summary: Ephemeral-proxy memory-spiral causing intermittent 5xx and elevated error rate during mixed embed/chat burst
description:
Issue summary:
During a mixed embedding + chat workload ramp from a single dedicated tenant (AtlasAI) we observed a persistent elevation in 5xx errors served by the API gateway and increased upstream runtime retries. Error rate rose from baseline ~0.4% to ~4.8% over a 20 minute window and remained elevated despite normal GPU utilization on Dedicated nodes.

Impact:
- Customer (AtlasAI) reporting degraded user experience: failed generation calls and truncated streaming sessions.
- Elevated 5xxs observed across both generation and embedding routes for the tenant; other tenants in the same region saw minor bump but returned to baseline.
- Business: P1 customer impact for a dedicated tenant.

Environment:
- prod: us-west region (us-west-2).
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embeddings/batch.
- Customer tier: dedicated.

Initial observations / telemetry:
- Grafana: api-gateway 502/503 spikes coincident with accept-queue growth on ephemeral-proxy pool (proxy-ephemeral-usw-3).
- Memory heap size for ephemeral-proxy processes increased steadily between 03:12-03:32 UTC; RSS grew by ~40% before process restart.
- Accept queue latency and proxy event-loop stalls correlating with SYN backlog growth.
- Serving runtime logs: increased connection resets and 504s when proxy accepted but upstream timed out.
- No comparable GPU OOMs or serving-runtime panics in the dedicated GPU fleet.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Run mixed workload: small-batch embedding uploads + concurrent streaming chat sessions pinned to customer routing.
2) After sustained burst (~350 RPS mixed for ~10 minutes), ephemeral-proxy memory begins to grow and connection handling degrades.
3) API gateway surfaces 502/503; some upstreams show timeouts and hedged retry amplification.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Ephemeral-proxy has a memory regression triggered by specific request mix (multipart embedding + streaming headers). Heap growth pattern suggests a leak or retention in the proxy request buffer when multiple chunked/streaming requests interleave.
- Hypothesis 2: Slow accept queue processing due to event-loop stalls leads to head-of-line delays; when proxies are near their soft memory limit the process delays cause upstream timeouts and API gateway to mark upstream unhealthy.
- Queries used: Kibana search "service:ephemeral-proxy AND env:prod AND region:us-west AND container:"proxy" | sort @timestamp" and Grafana panel "api-gateway accept-queue depth by proxy pool".
- Relevant logs: (excerpt)
  [2026-03-14T03:18:05Z] proxy.ephemeral INFO accept_queue_depth=112 event_loop_delay_ms=1240 rss_bytes=1342177280
  [2026-03-14T03:18:06Z] proxy.ephemeral WARN request=chunked_upload id=txn_9f7 stall_ms=980 retained_buffers=23
  [2026-03-14T03:20:14Z] apigw ERROR upstream=proxy-ephemeral-usw-3 status=502 retry=true

Mitigations applied so far:
- Immediate: scaled ephemeral-proxy pool +2 instances for pool proxy-ephemeral-usw-3 at 03:28 UTC (temporarily reduced accept-queue pressure).
- Applied temporary traffic steering: routed AtlasAI traffic to alternate proxy pool (proxy-ephemeral-usw-5) at 03:34 UTC. Error rate dropped from 4.8% -> 1.2% after steering but did not fully return to baseline.
- Rolling restarts: restarted 3/6 ephemeral-proxy processes in the affected pool to reclaim memory.

Open actions / next steps:
- Engineering: reproduce locally with synthetic workload combining chunked embedding uploads and streaming to replicate memory growth. (Assigned to Miguel Torres).
- Runtime: add additional diagnostic allocation traces to ephemeral-proxy to capture retained buffer histograms and event-loop latencies. (Tentative patch/PR #5120).
- Ops: monitor accept-queue and event-loop delay panels for 2 hours; enable auto-steer policy for pools hitting sustained event-loop-delay > 500ms.
- CS: notify AtlasAI of mitigations and temporary routing; track customer impact and collect example request IDs.

Resolution notes (in-progress):
- Temporary mitigation (traffic steering + restarts) reduced error rate but a code fix is required. A PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5120) contains an initial patch to free retained chunk buffers sooner; tests are queued.
- If reproduced in staging with dev-alloc tracing, plan a canary deploy to prod pool with extended observability for 6 hours before rolling to all pools.
steps_to_reproduce: Run mixed workload: small-batch embedding uploads concurrently with streaming chat sessions
Sustain burst ~300-400 RPS for 8-12 minutes pinned to a single tenant routing
Observe ephemeral-proxy pool accept-queue depth and RSS growth via Grafana
